# Manage Many Game Objects {#sec-ch10}

::: {.chapter-banner}

[GAME 10 | Breakout]{.game-title}

[Objects]{.skill-chip} [Arrays]{.skill-chip} [Loops]{.skill-chip}

:::

::: {.callout-note .code-guide title="How to use the code pieces" icon="false"}

The short snippets below explain individual rules. The complete browser example later in this chapter combines them into a playable page.

:::

::: {.callout-tip .mission title="Your mission" icon="false"}

By the end of this chapter, you can:

- store many objects in an array
- use loops to update and draw objects
- remove or mark hit bricks
- understand basic collision tests

:::

::: {.callout-note .big-idea title="The big idea" icon="false"}

Breakout has many bricks. We do not want 30 separate variables. Arrays let one variable hold a whole collection of game objects.

:::

## Store bricks as objects

Each brick can be an object with position, size, and whether it is still active.

![Collision detection asks whether game objects overlap.](../figures/chapter_08/collision-overlap.png){#fig-ch10 fig-alt="Two rectangles partially overlap; the shared area illustrates a rectangular collision test." width="100%"}

**Read the picture:** A collision is not just being close. The shapes overlap horizontally **and** vertically. The picture uses rectangles; the beginner ball test uses a square bounding box around the ball.

```javascript
const bricks = [
  { x: 20, y: 20, w: 60, h: 20, alive: true },
  { x: 90, y: 20, w: 60, h: 20, alive: true },
  { x: 160, y: 20, w: 60, h: 20, alive: true }
];
```

## Loop through the array

`for...of` gives us each brick one at a time.

```javascript
for (const brick of bricks) {
  if (brick.alive) {
    ctx.fillRect(brick.x, brick.y, brick.w, brick.h);
  }
}
```

## A simple collision test

A ball hits a brick when its position overlaps the brick rectangle. For a beginner version, we can use the ball center plus its radius.

```javascript
function hitsBrick(ballX, ballY, r, brick) {
  return (
    ballX + r > brick.x &&
    ballX - r < brick.x + brick.w &&
    ballY + r > brick.y &&
    ballY - r < brick.y + brick.h
  );
}
```

## Change the world after a hit

When a collision happens, mark the brick as no longer alive and reverse the vertical direction of the ball.

```javascript
if (brick.alive && hitsBrick(x, y, radius, brick)) {
  brick.alive = false;
  dy = -dy;
  score++;
}
```

## Play Breakout in your browser {.unnumbered}

Save this page as `index.html`, or open `workspace/chapter10-breakout/index.html`. Each brick is an object in the `bricks` array. The loop draws only active bricks and tests the ball against them.

[COMPLETE EXAMPLE | `index.html`]{.code-label}

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Breakout Practice</title>
  <style>
    body { margin: 0; min-height: 100vh; display: grid; place-items: center; background: #fff3e8; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; color: #17243b; }
    main { padding: 24px; border: 3px solid #17243b; border-radius: 18px; background: white; }
    h1 { margin: 0 0 8px; color: #c04a5a; }
    canvas { display: block; border: 2px solid #17243b; background: #17243b; }
    #status { min-height: 1.5em; margin-bottom: 0; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <main>
    <h1>Breakout Practice</h1>
    <p>Hold ← or → to move the paddle and catch the ball.</p>
    <canvas id="game" width="560" height="360"></canvas>
    <p id="status">Bricks cleared: 0</p>
  </main>
  <script>
    const canvas = document.getElementById("game");
    const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
    const status = document.getElementById("status");
    const keys = {};
    window.addEventListener("keydown", e => {
      if (e.key === "ArrowLeft" || e.key === "ArrowRight") e.preventDefault();
      keys[e.key] = true;
    });
    window.addEventListener("keyup", e => { keys[e.key] = false; });
    window.addEventListener("blur", () => {
      keys.ArrowLeft = false;
      keys.ArrowRight = false;
    });

    const bricks = [
      { x: 45, y: 40, w: 100, h: 22, alive: true },
      { x: 165, y: 40, w: 100, h: 22, alive: true },
      { x: 285, y: 40, w: 100, h: 22, alive: true },
      { x: 405, y: 40, w: 100, h: 22, alive: true },
      { x: 45, y: 76, w: 100, h: 22, alive: true },
      { x: 165, y: 76, w: 100, h: 22, alive: true },
      { x: 285, y: 76, w: 100, h: 22, alive: true },
      { x: 405, y: 76, w: 100, h: 22, alive: true }
    ];
    let paddleX = 230;
    const paddleY = 330, paddleW = 100, paddleH = 12;
    let x = 280, y = 250, dx = 3, dy = -3;
    const radius = 10;
    let score = 0;

    function hitsBrick(ballX, ballY, r, brick) {
      return (
        ballX + r > brick.x &&
        ballX - r < brick.x + brick.w &&
        ballY + r > brick.y &&
        ballY - r < brick.y + brick.h
      );
    }

    function update() {
      if (keys.ArrowLeft) paddleX -= 6;
      if (keys.ArrowRight) paddleX += 6;
      paddleX = Math.max(0, Math.min(canvas.width - paddleW, paddleX));
      x += dx;
      y += dy;
      if (x < radius || x > canvas.width - radius) dx = -dx;
      if (y < radius) dy = Math.abs(dy);
      if (dy > 0 && y + radius >= paddleY && y - radius <= paddleY + paddleH &&
          x + radius >= paddleX && x - radius <= paddleX + paddleW) {
        y = paddleY - radius;
        dy = -Math.abs(dy);
      }
      for (const brick of bricks) {
        if (brick.alive && hitsBrick(x, y, radius, brick)) {
          brick.alive = false;
          dy = -dy;
          score++;
          status.textContent = "Bricks cleared: " + score;
          break;
        }
      }
      if (y > canvas.height + radius) {
        x = canvas.width / 2;
        y = 250;
        dy = -3;
        status.textContent = "Try again! Bricks cleared: " + score;
      }
    }

    function draw() {
      ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
      ctx.fillStyle = "#17243b";
      ctx.fillRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
      for (const brick of bricks) {
        if (brick.alive) {
          ctx.fillStyle = brick.y === 40 ? "#f899b5" : "#ffe48a";
          ctx.fillRect(brick.x, brick.y, brick.w, brick.h);
        }
      }
      ctx.fillStyle = "#8ce3ff";
      ctx.fillRect(paddleX, paddleY, paddleW, paddleH);
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.arc(x, y, radius, 0, Math.PI * 2);
      ctx.fillStyle = "white";
      ctx.fill();
    }

    function loop() {
      update();
      draw();
      requestAnimationFrame(loop);
    }
    draw();
    requestAnimationFrame(loop);
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```

The demonstration pages pause automatic animation and place the ball for one or three known brick collisions. The playable page keeps animating normally.

![Breakout Practice in Chrome before a brick is hit.](../figures/chapter_10/breakout-start.png){#fig-ch10-breakout-start fig-alt="A Breakout canvas shows eight colored bricks, a ball, a paddle, and Bricks cleared: 0." width="100%"}
![Breakout Practice in Chrome after one brick collision.](../figures/chapter_10/breakout-one-hit.png){#fig-ch10-breakout-one fig-alt="One top-row brick is missing and the page says Bricks cleared: 1." width="100%"}
![Breakout Practice in Chrome after three brick collisions.](../figures/chapter_10/breakout-three-hits.png){#fig-ch10-breakout-three fig-alt="Three top-row bricks are missing and the page says Bricks cleared: 3." width="100%"}

**Read the pictures:** `hitsBrick()` finds an overlap, then the code sets that brick's `alive` property to false. The next draw skips it, so a gap appears in the row. The score rises from zero to one, then three. The brick object stays in the array even though it is no longer drawn or hit.

::: {.callout-note .advanced-study title="Advanced Study | Objects, arrays, and collision logic" icon="false" collapse="false"}

[OPTIONAL DEEPER DIVE]{.study-badge}

An object groups properties that belong to one game object. An array stores many objects in order. A common rectangle collision test checks whether one rectangle is not completely left, right, above, or below the other. Larger games often separate `update()`, `draw()`, and collision functions.

```javascript
const brick = { x: 40, y: 20, w: 60, h: 20, alive: true };
bricks.push(brick);
```

**Each object is one brick; the array is the collection.** `brick.alive = false` changes a property on that brick. A `for...of` loop can visit the collection when checking collisions and when drawing.

**Know the approximation.** `hitsBrick` checks the square around the ball against the brick. At a corner, those squares can overlap before the circle itself touches. A fast ball can also jump past a thin brick between frames.

**One hit, one response.** Avoid reversing the ball repeatedly for several bricks in one update. A simple first approach is to stop checking after the first detected hit.

:::
